XXIII.}}</noinclude>{{verse|chapter=23|verse=17}} And he of nece{{ls}}sitie had to relea{{ls}}e vnto them vpon the fea{{ls}}t day, one. {{verse|chapter=23|verse=18}} But the vvhole multitude together cried out, {{ls}}aying, Di{{ls}}patch him, and relea{{ls}}e vs Barabbas. {{verse|chapter=23|verse=19}} vvho vvas for a certaine {{ls}}edition made in the citie and murder, ca{{ls}}t into pri{{ls}}on. {{verse|chapter=23|verse=20}} And Pilate againe {{ls}}pake to them, de{{ls}}irous to relea{{ls}}e {{sc|Iesvs}}. {{verse|chapter=23|verse=21}} But they cried againe, {{ls}}aying, Crucifie, crucifie him. {{verse|chapter=23|verse=22}} And he the third time {{ls}}aid to them, VVhy, vvhat euil hath this man done? I finde no cau{{ls}}e of death in him. I vvil correct him therfore and let him goe. {{verse|chapter=23|verse=23}} But they vvere in{{ls}}tant vvith loude voices requiring that he might be crucified. And their voices preuailed. {{verse|chapter=23|verse=24}} And Pilate adiudged their petition to be done. {{verse|chapter=23|verse=25}} And he relea{{ls}}ed vnto them him that for murder and {{ls}}edition had been ca{{ls}}t into pri{{ls}}on, vvhom they demaunded: but {{sc|Iesvs}} he deliuered to their plea{{ls}}ure.

{{verse|chapter=23|verse=26}} And vvhen they led him, they tooke one Simon of Cyréne comming from the countrie: and they laid the cro{{ls}}{{ls}}e vpon him to carie after {{sc|Iesvs}}. {{verse|chapter=23|verse=27}} And there folovved him a great multitude of people, and of vvomen vvhich bevvailed and lamented him. {{verse|chapter=23|verse=28}} But {{sc|Iesvs}} turning to them, {{ls}}aid, Daughters of Hieru{{ls}}alem, vveepe not vpon me, but vveepe vpon your {{ls}}elues, and vpon your children. {{verse|chapter=23|verse=29}} For behold the daies {{ls}}hal come, vvherein they vvil {{ls}}ay, Ble{{ls}}sed are the barren, and the vvombes that haue not borne, and the pappes that haue not giuen {{ls}}ucke. {{verse|chapter=23|verse=30}} {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=''Os. 10, 8.''}}* ''Then {{ls}}hal they begin to {{ls}}ay to the mountaines, Fal vpon vs: and to the hilles, Couer vs''. {{verse|chapter=23|verse=31}} For if in the greene wood they doe the{{ls}}e things, in the drie vvhat {{ls}}hal be done?

{{verse|chapter=23|verse=32}} And there vvere led al{{ls}}o other tvvo malefactours vvith him, to be executed. {{verse|chapter=23|verse=33}} And after they came to the place vvhich is called Caluarie, there they crucified him: and the theeues, one on the right hand, and the other on the left. {{verse|chapter=23|verse=34}} And {{sc|Iesvs}} {{ls}}aid, Father, {{sup|‖}} forgiue them, for they knovv not vvhat they doe. But they deuiding his garments, did ca{{ls}}t lottes.

{{verse|chapter=23|verse=35}} And the people {{ls}}toode {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=''`beholding'',}}`expecting', and the princes vvith them derided him, {{ls}}aying, Others he hath {{ls}}aued, let him {{ls}}aue him {{ls}}elf, if this be Chri{{ls}}t, the elect of God. {{verse|chapter=23|verse=36}} And the {{ls}}ouldiars al{{ls}}o mocked him comming to him, and offering him vinegre, {{verse|chapter=23|verse=37}} {{ls}}aying, If thou be the king of the Ievves, {{ls}}aue thy {{ls}}elf. {{verse|chapter=23|verse=38}} And there vvas al{{ls}}o a {{ls}}uper{{ls}}cription vvritten ouer him in Greeke, and Latine, and Hebrevv letters:<noinclude>{{rh|||{{sc|This}}}}</noinclude>
